questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had always wanted to try and live in the US, and I had heard a lot of good things about Boston, because it is such a big university city. I did a lot of research and decided that Boston was one of the destinations I was most interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I wrote a lot to Sage Suorsa, the exchange coordinator from BU, and she was usually very fast at answering. But from Copenhagen University it was a little more difficult, the coordinator wasn't very helpful. There was a zoom meeting for exchange students a few weeks before the semester started, and there they made a whatsapp group with everybody. Then there was a lot of events in the first week, though they were mostly for freshmen, but we went to them to meet new people. I had met the other danish exchanges students from KU and also from CBS in the week before school started.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received all the information about school start, covid, all the events and activities, orientation, moving-in etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I wish they would have had a specific event just for international students, because we were older than the freshmen so the events weren't always so fun.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Apartment style, single dorm, double dorm, triple and quadruple dorm. 
I lived in an apartment style dorm where we had each our room, but the kitchen was in my roommates room. And we also had our own bathroom. I was really lucky with my housing, my roommate was also a senior, and had lived in that apartment the year before. It was located on Beacon St., so really close to the center of campus, but also next to the T, Target and Fenway.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my apartment there was a kitchen, but I didn't use it very much because it was inside my roommates room. When you live in apartment style, you don't have to buy a mealplan, but I ended up choosing the apartment style mealplan, because my friends all ate at the dining hall, so it was nice to be able to join them. So I ate maybe 4 dinners a week at dining hall, and breakfast at home and lunch either madpakke from home or at GSU. The kitchen in the apartment was very nice, but there are no cutlery, dishes etc. so I was lucky that my roommate had everything and let me use it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a gamble. Some of my friends got very bad dorms - very small and with roommates that they couldn't get along with. It is very expensive, but I think it is worth it. They told us it was very unlikely that exchange students got apartment style, but I put it as my priority 1 anyways, and was lucky that I got it assigned. It is more expensive than dorm style, but you save the mealplan. But it was also quite hard to find things off-campus, I would definitely recommend looking for something more than 2 weeks before arriving, if you want to live off-campus. Some people off-campus had very nice places, but then it was also quite far away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think on-campus is worth it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am on the bachelor, so I had to get one course, Game Theory, in order to get the credit at home, so I was a bit nervous because once we got access to registration it was already full. But then you just have to check everyday for people to drop out and it happens often, so one day in the summer, I was able to get a spot. Same with the other courses I wanted. It was nice that you could register for more courses than you wanted, and cancel them after they had already started, if you were unsure.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On StudentLink you click register and choose the class you want. You can look up the classes on BUs website before and find the code.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I tried to write to my professors if there wasn't a spot available, but they couldn't do anything because of covid rules, they weren't very flexible about letting extra people join.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted. 
Game Theory: wasn't my favorite professor. But interesting courses. 
Behavioral Economics with Prof. Fisman was very good! 
International Economics I was a "prioriteret valgfag", which was very interesting, but it was evening school and only 4 people on the course, which I didn't know before getting there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just keep checking all the time if there is a class which is full, even after the semester has started, because a lot of people drop out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Definitely easier than economics at KU, but still very interesting and different way of teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 300 classes and one 400 class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different - there are midterms, sometimes several, which forces you to study the material early on in the course, which I liked. I also almost didn't have any assignments, which is very different from my courses at KU. Instead there were pop up quizzes and attendance/participation was 5/10% of your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game Theory
Behavioral Economics
International Economics I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Behavioral Economics, it was definitely my favorite courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Ubers and going out. It can be quite expensive to go out in Boston, and the public transportation doesn't work after 1, so we always had to take ubers home. But they aren't too expensive when shared.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport card (CharlieCard) - don't buy it! It costs $300 and I definitely didn't use it enough. Instead you can get a bluebike subscription.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is pretty much a club for any interest you have, so that was very nice! I attended the women in economics club and the knitting club. It was a nice way of meeting Americans.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are over 400 clubs, and there is a free gym which was very good. Hockey games are fun too.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You should join sports classes at Fitrec and join clubs at Splash. I can really recommend going to a Tailgate at Boston College and then seeing the football match. Also baseball at Fenway, and going on trips to NYC, Cape Cod.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to NYC twice, it costs only 300kr roundtrip with Flixbus and it was very fun. Cape Cod is very beautiful too.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Boston is a very international city. It was fun to experience the things I had seen in movies and TV in real life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was kind of hard to get to know local students, but if your classes has group projects that is a good way! Or at the clubs too. I was mostly with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness of the American people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Summer clothes!! It was so much hotter than I thought it would be.
Raincoat.
A danish "stikdåse" - so you can use your regular chargers, but just put an adapter on the stikdåse.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my new friends and challenging myself by leaving everything behind and traveling by myself so far away, especially during covid where it wasn't easy to travel back and forth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the first week in Boston by myself before I met any people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
